I try to let each vintage speak for itself with minimal interference. By using organic farming methods and leaving our wines unfiltered and unfined, the beauty of the fruit shows through.” —Eric Hays, Winemaker VISIT US Château Davell welcomes you and your friends for daily visits. VISIT VINEYARD Learn more about our organic and biodynamic vineyard. VINEYARD BUY WINE Shop our handcrafted, small-batch wines online today. SHOP ABOUT CHÂTEAU DAVELL VINEYARDS Château Davell's Estate Vineyard is situated at a 3000' elevation in the El Dorado AVA. We use sustainable vineyard management methods, eliminating the need for conventional herbicides and pesticides, and supporting the vitality of the surrounding ecosystem. We use cover cropping and other natural farming techniques in our estate vineyard. Our soils are made up of rich clay, decomposed granite, and volcanic rock making it the perfect place to grow grapes. We are thankful to have relationships with other sustainable and organic growers in both El Dorado and Lodi Counties to source additional quality fruit for our winemaking. Pictured here is our vineyard nestled among the beautiful pines of our region. WINES Château Davell produces handcrafted wines in extremely small lots, combining old-world methods with new-world style. Winemaker/Owner Eric Hays approaches winemaking more as an artist than a scientist. He strives to make all of our wines, from our signature red blends to our Zander Zinfandel and Davell Cabernet Franc, well balanced, smooth, rich and velvety. Because none of our wines are filtered or fined, they have a beautifully pronounced bouquet, flavor and body not found in mass produced wines. Our labels feature the winemaker's paintings of our family members and the original artwork used for the labels is on display in the Tasting Room. FAMILY Being able to spend time together as a family is a really important element of our business. Eric developed a passion for wine during his 15-year tenure as a restaurant and club manager, and honed his winemaking skills on the job as an Assistant Winemaker at a local winery. If you're lucky you might find the winery's namesake Davell and her husband Terry behind the bar pouring wine. With some hope the kids Charlotte and Auguste pictured with Eric will take over operations some day. SUSTAINABILITY Living an eco-friendly lifestyle, being good stewards of the land we farm, and creating a healthy environment for our children and animals are all integral parts of our family philosophy and business practice. We use no herbicides, pesticides or chemical fertilizers. Bottling by hand using recycled-content glass, labels produced with 100% post-consumer waste papers, and FSC Certified corks helps keep our production and packaging as sustainable as possible. We never add dyes or fining agents to our wines and we strive to work with other local growers using organic farming practices whenever possible. Thank you for letting us share our passion with you, and for supporting our family business! CHÂTEAU DAVELL EVENTS OUR TASTING ROOM Château Davell's daily tasting menu varies, but always showcases six of our current vintages of unique varietals and blends, each paired with a different local / farmstead cheese or other pairing. Our reserve wines, as well as some library vintages are also available for purchase at the Tasting Room, along with an assortment of artisan picnic supplies and hand-crafted chocolates. Our seasonal hard apple cider, Avery Sparkling Rosé and Cuvee Blanc, all on tap, are only available by the glass at the Tasting Room. Stay and enjoy our wines by the glass or bottle in one of our relaxing picnic areas. EXPLORE ARE YOU OF LEGAL DRINKING AGE? YES NO TEXAS WHISKEY, MADE FROM THE GRAIN UP Herman Marshall is an independently owned Texas whiskey distillery founded in 2010 by Master Distiller Herman Beckley and his business partner Marshall Louis. The name comes from their first names (here’s the story). When it opened in Garland, it was the first legal distillery in Dallas County since Prohibition. Today the Herman Marshall tasting room at 121 N. Ballard Ave. in historic downtown Wylie, TX pours our straight bourbon, straight rye, single malt, Generation Gin and Dry County vodka, alongside seasonal and classic cocktails, with weekly trivia, poker, bingo and live music. Address: 121 N. Ballard Ave., Wylie, TX 75098 Phone: 469-304-0069 Hours: Tuesday–Thursday 4pm–10pm, Friday 2pm–midnight, Saturday noon–midnight; closed Sunday and Monday Founded: 2010, as the first legal distillery in Dallas County since Prohibition Made with: grain from Texas farms; our bourbon, rye and single malt are aged at least four years in new American white oak barrels with a #2 char Nearby: an easy drive from Plano, Sachse, Murphy, Rockwall, Garland, Lucas and Lavon FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS Where is Herman Marshall located? Our tasting room is at 121 N. Ballard Ave. in historic downtown Wylie, TX, a short drive from Plano, Sachse, Murphy, Rockwall, Lavon and Lucas. What kind of whiskey does Herman Marshall make? Small-batch straight bourbon, straight rye and single malt, plus single barrel, bottled-in-bond and cask strength releases. We also make Dry County American Whiskey, Dry County Texas Vodka and Generation Gin. New to whiskey? Start with Bourbon vs. Rye vs. Single Malt. Can I buy Herman Marshall whiskey online? Bottles are sold at the tasting room, or you can order online and pick up at the tasting room. Texas law doesn’t allow us to ship bottles within Texas, and sales are limited to four bottles per person per month. You can also find our whiskey at the stores on our Where to Buy page. Is Herman Marshall a bar? Yes. Our tasting room in downtown Wylie is a full bar pouring cocktails and our own whiskey, gin and vodka, with a 500-square-foot patio. We host trivia, Texas Hold’em poker, bingo and live music. Can I rent Herman Marshall for a private event? Yes. Our 2,780-square-foot upstairs event space includes seating, tables and audio/visual access, cocktails are available from our bar, and you can bring your own caterer. cdq1cwb.txt: Bad Tom Smith Brewing | Bad Ass In A Glass | Social media links | Bad Tom Smith Brewing | Main navigation | Bad Tom Smith Brewing | BTS Pint Glass | Our Brews | Bad Tom Smith Brewery | Bad Tom Smith Brewing Food | Our Bourbons | Footer social media links | Bad Tom Smith Brewing brings its quality brewed craft beers and bourbons to the Cincinnati via our comfortable brewery & tap room. | Bad Tom Smith Brewing | Bad Ass In A Glass | Bad Tom Smith Brewing | BAD ASS IN A GLASS FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TIKTOK BREWERY & TAP ROOM INFORMATION Beers On Tap BOURBON & COCKTAILS FOOD MENU & TAKE OUT EVENTS BAD TOM SMITH BEERS BAD TOM SMITH BEERS BAD ASS IN A CAN CANNED BEER BOURBON BAD TOM SMITH BOURBON MERCHANDISE MERCHANDISE ABOUT OUR STORY TALE OF BAD TOM Blog Contact BAD ASS IN A GLASS Bad Tom Smith Brewing We all have a story. Ours starts with an outlaw, his distant relative who learned how to brew #BadAssInAGlass, and ends with a taste that makes you slow life down enough to make friends with a stranger. Our craft beers are who we are, lets you know where we’re from, and gives us a chance to hang with you. Registration is closed See other events Time & Location June 27 at 12pm, 2pm and 4pm (2 & 4pm FULL) Taste of Santa Rita Hills, 2923 Grand Ave, Los Olivos, CA 93441, USA About the event For the first time, we are thrilled to welcome winemaker Don Schroeder to our tasting room for an event where you can taste the latest bottlings of Sea Smoke Pinot Noir and Chardonnay, plus the exciting re-release of Botella! The quality of the Sea Smoke Estate bottlings has undoubtedly increased the notoriety of the Sta. Rita Hills AVA since their first vintage in 2001. When Don joined Sea Smoke in 2003, he worked alongside legendary winemaker Kris Curran and rose up the ranks to become principal winemaker in 2008, and as of 2024 serves as Director of Winemaking. Through each vintage, he has ensured the consistent character, sophistication and complexity of the wines. The 2023 vintage was nothing short of magical -- the long growing season was preceded by rainfall and finished with a warm push toward ripening just before harvest. The result in the 2023 estate wines is a luxurious core of fruit with graceful purity, soaring flavors and the structure and sophistication for an exciting evolution in the years ahead. Botella was first unveiled in 2001 as an enticing preview of each vintage while Sea Smoke's flagship estate wines patiently came of age. Produced until 2014, Botella was then retired as every cluster of estate fruit became dedicated to Southing and Ten. Now, after a 12-year hiatus, Botella is reborn! Sourced from exceptional neighboring vineyards in the Sta. Rita Hills, these wines feature earlier picks and shorter aging regimes that allow both the Pinot Noir and Chardonnay to showcase their bright aromatics and vibrant energy. Join us for this premier opportunity to taste Sea Smoke Estate and Botella bottlings with Don on Saturday, June 27. Three seatings are available for these educational tastings at 12:00 pm, 2:00 pm and 4:00 pm (2pm and 4pm seatings are full). Reservations and a $50 fee are required to hold your seat. This fee can be applied to $350+ bottle purchases at the event. Refreshing like a seltzer - History Ruzzo was created by a family and close friends who were motivated to create a sense of togetherness during the heart of the pandemic. Our close knit family decided to brave the unknown in hopes to reach a community that needed something different. What started as a beloved beverage turned into Ruzzo- A way for people to unite and embrace a carefree lifestyle. TAPROOM INFO EVENTS About Us The Ruzzo family is made up of highly motivated people, dedicated to inspiring and bringing people together with our new beverage category we created - Ruzzo's Hard Citrus. It's light and bubbly with great flavor and a refreshing finish. Our mission is to educate the world on our unique drink and bring a brand new innovative product to the people. It all started out with making beer. Then came hard cider. Next it was seltzer. Now, the new revolution: Ruzzo's Hard Citrus. RUZZO [roo-zoh} A Carefree Way Of Life Indulge in carefree experiences with us. However, stepping outside the usual selections can make for a more […] Celebrating Oregon’s Finest Winemakers Oregon has earned a reputation for producing world-class wines, particularly Pinot Noir and Chardonnay, thanks to the dedication of […] Home Wine Shops in Portland Portland’s Hawthorne area is home to several local wine shops dedicated to offering high-quality, limited-production wines from around the world. These shops often focus on sourcing hand-crafted wines from wineries and estates known for their commitment to excellence. Curated Wine Selection Many wine shops in Portland carefully choose their selections to ensure they represent the best in their category for both quality and value. These shops proudly showcase some of the finest and rarest Oregon Pinot Noir producers from the Willamette Valley, alongside a diverse selection of wines from global regions. Wines from Local and Global Regions In addition to their focus on local wines, Portland wine shops offer an extensive range of wines from prominent wine regions worldwide. Whether you’re seeking Bordeaux, Burgundy, wines from the Loire Valley, Italy, Austria, Germany, or top selections from California and the Pacific Northwest, there are plenty of options available. This variety allows customers to discover wines that suit their tastes no matter the origin. In addition to international selections, Portland wine shops take pride in their local offerings. A highlight of many shops is their specialization in Oregon Pinot Noir. Through close relationships with some of the Willamette Valley’s smallest, most quality-driven producers, these shops offer rare and exclusive selections. Many of these wines are produced in extremely limited quantities and are rarely available outside Oregon. For those seeking personalized recommendations, Portland wine shops are also known for building strong relationships with their customers. By understanding individual tastes and preferences, staff can recommend wines that align with each person’s palate. This personalized approach allows wine enthusiasts to explore a wide variety of flavors and styles. Copyright mttaborfinewines.com 2026

Sourcing Our Wines Our Grapes are sourced by "Winexpert" The Winexpert Quality Story: “From Vineyard to Glass” "Winexpert’s commitment to excellence, and dedication to delivering the highest quality products in the winemaking market, has made us the world’s foremost supplier of premium wine juices. Our careful sourcing of supply, combined with state-of-the-art processing facilities and stringent quality control procedures continue to set the industry standard. Our dedication to product excellence began over 20 years ago and continues today as we source high quality grape juice and concentrate from the world’s best wine regions. We strive for quality at every level in our operation, seeking to bring the finest these wine regions have to offer right to our customers’ glass. Great wine is not made in a factory; it is made in the vineyard, where sunshine, good soil and careful tending make great grapes. We regularly visit with our growers and suppliers and have stringent quality specifications and standards to ensure that we get the best possible varietals. We are offered many different grape juices and concentrates every year, but we make certain we select only the best available for our customers. Everyone that represents Winexpert strives to positively affect quality at every level, from the vineyard to the glass, so that you can make the best wine possible – every single time!" Featured Products About Us Our History I started in the wine making business at the age of 4, helping my grandfather by crushing grapes. My love for wine making returned in 1990 when I started making my own homemade wines and Limoncello. In 2020, along with my wife Janis, we perfected our recipes and decided to start our own Micro Winery. My License was granted by the Liquor Control Board in June of 2022 and so begins my new venture in Beautiful Bucks County Pennsylvania. While founders Mitch and Ashley Miller both enjoy full time careers outside of the distilled spirits industry, their vision was to start a small family owned distillery in their hometown of Warsaw, IN to serve the local community. The foundation to Mitch’s passion for starting a family owned business was laid at a young age growing up around his parent’s business - Miller & Sons Tool & Die (now Instru-med). After graduating from Ball State University’s Entrepreneurship program in 2003, and gaining experience in various industries over the years, the idea for Streven was born. Ashley continues her work as a Doctor of Physical Therapy while also managing the Miller Household of 5 kids, including 2 sets of twins. strȇv'ǝn The inspiration for the name Streven comes from the Dutch word strēven, or to strive, aim, endeavor, aspire, or try. This is the essence of Streven - our commitment to creating the highest quality spirits for our customers. Never cutting corners, and using methods and quality ingredients to produce spirits we are proud of. Spirits All Streven spirits are distilled and bottled on-site at the distillery. Our grains are sourced from Indiana producers including corn, rye, and malted barley. Careful attention is paid during the distillation process to only use the “heart” cut of the distillate – resulting in a cleaner, brighter product. The Hammen Family Orchard & Winery, established in August 2018, is a family-owned and operated enterprise. We specialize in fresh produce, cider, and wine, all crafted from locally sourced ingredients, with many sourced directly from our own orchard. Our orchard, winery, and cider mill are committed to producing and offering products of the highest quality. Additionally, we have an on-site gift shop where we offer a variety of our products, wines, and local favorites. Learn More What We Offer ​ Customer satisfaction is our foremost priority. We aim for you and your family to appreciate each item you purchase from us as much as we valued its creation. Our extensive range of options ensures that you can find precisely what you seek. Winery We produce wine, mead, and hard cider on site using entirely homegrown and locally sourced fruit and honey. At our wine bar, you can enjoy a wine tasting and wine, mead, and hard cider by the glass. If you find something you like, we have bottles of all of our available varieties in our store. Orchard We grow over 250 varieties of apples, many of which are old heirloom varieties, along with peaches, and various other fruits. We sell fresh produce in season and sweet cider that we produce right on site. We also do custom cider pressing by appointment. Cider Mill We have an onsite cider press and offer apple pressing by appointment. Plese contact us if you are looking to setup a cider press appointment. Gift Shop Our storefront gift shop is where you will find apple cider vinegar, preserves and canned goods, cheese, crackers, mugs and glasses, soaps, lotions, and various other items, most of which are locally made. Shop Wine What People Are Saying! We love to hear from happy customers what you thought of our wine or your visit! Please leave us a review! Leave A Review! What a fun and relaxing way to spend a Sunday afternoon. Thank you, Amber, for sharing truly unique and interesting wines with us! Carrie Nation wielded a hatchet to smash saloons as the figurehead of the Temperance movement that would eventually lead to the 18th amendment and prohibition. With the 21st amendment, we repealed that poor decision in our country’s history. Carrie Nation never lived to see that day, and is buried right here in Belton Missouri. With that kind of history in our back yard, many have mixed feelings. Look – we just want to bury the hatchet on this local connection and have a few craft beers to show there are no hard feelings. We’re opening Broken Hatchet Brewing in historic downtown Belton and celebrating our community. We’re brewing up classic styles of beer as well as a few thought provoking beers, so ask us about the reasoning behind our beer names. We’re located downtown in the old Cass County library that helped educate the community from 1975-2003. It’s also an excuse to mix in a few witty library and education metaphors. Dewey Decimal IPA anyone? #BrewedInBelton Brad & Cara Broken Hatchet Brewing CONTACT US BROKEN HATCHET BREWERY Let us know how we are doing. We welcome suggestions from our customers to continue to provide the best experience possible. Hit the trail to the winery and cidery for a one-of-a-kind backwoods adventure. Traveling along Ridge Road? Keep an eye out for the marked sign! From the west (Winn Road): Turn left (south) at the sign. From the east (Ames Road): Turn right (south) at the sign. The trail winds through the rugged beauty of the Maine Highlands, following a scenic ridgeline. Along the way, enjoy sweeping views and a peaceful overlook of Ricker Pond. Come relax, take in the views, say hello to the goats, and join us for a tasting—whether it's a flight, a glass, or a bottle of wine, or a 64 oz. growler of your favorite hard cider to take home. We’re not a big-box winery or cidery. We’re passionate about craft fermenta—small-batch wines and hard ciders made with care, creativity, and a commitment to quality over quantity. Our tasting room lineup changes from week to week, with fresh flavors and new profiles often making their debut alongside our core selections. We're always dreaming up new combinations just waiting for you to discover. From traditional grape wines to fruit, berry, citrus, honey (mead), maple syrup, and other specialty creations, there's always something unique on the menu. With the exception being that we are not making these wines with any personality, we are making them as "portraits" of our three daughters, intricately planned and executed. A painstaking process in selecting clones that would match the unique character of each, paired with individually custom made barrels and finishing with meticulous winemaking. We exclusively use copper stills, including both column and pot stills. Some of our fermentation process lasts over a month, ensuring a rich and complex flavor profile. By utilizing a slow distillation process, we enhance reflux and copper contact, resulting in a smoother spirit through meticulous smaller cuts. We also distill a minimum of 3 times (triple distill) our spirits. We age our premium craft spirits in some of the finest American oak casks, employing barrels of various sizes (5, 10, 15, 30, 53, and 100 gallons). The staves for our casks are seasoned for 12 to 48 months, depending on our suppliers. Additionally, we incorporate up to nine other types of wood for finishing, primarily for our rums and agave spirits. This unique approach places us among the few distilleries that operate this way, positioning us at the forefront of the maturation/finishing process. Today, we distill over 25 different products, making us one of the most versatile craft distilleries globally. Make A Tasting Room Reservation SOCIALLY RESPONSIBLE OPERATIONS We at NOCO Distillery believe in doing business that benefits not only us but the rest of the community as well. We outsource what processes we can to other local companies. For instance, we contract some of our wash to local breweries and complete the fermentation in our distillery. Which is not only efficient but also produces more work for the local community. As much as possible, we source raw materials from local producers. Much of the botanicals, fruits and grains we use in our craft spirits are produced right here in Colorado. By doing so, we reduce our operation’s carbon footprint; locally sourcing raw materials means a shorter distance to travel and thus lesser fuel consumption. It also maximizes our positive impact on the local economy. By purchasing from local businesses, we increase the income of local producers. This, in turn, provides locals with more work opportunities, directly or indirectly increases' locals' spending power (which boosts the local economy even more), and increases the government's tax earnings — the Colorado proud way. We also believe doing business and protecting the environment need not be mutually exclusive. Thus, we try to reduce the impact of our operation on the environment. We recycle or reuse most of everything we use in crafting our premium spirits. We also strive to be energy efficient; for instance, we use heat exchangers so that we can preheat succeeding batches, also use heat exchangers to heat the warehouse while distilling, which reduces our overall energy consumption significantly. During the winter months, we use a closed-circuit cooling system with water reclaimed from our Reverse Osmosis system. We also offer a recycle & reuse program where we provide a $0.50 credit for each bottle returned to us. We are apparently the only distillery in Colorado to offer it. Finally, we strive to use organic or Non-GMO raw materials, when possible, which, of course, depends on availability from our suppliers and will be indicated on our bottles. Founders Jim & Lynda Taylor and winemaker Ryan Taylor own the largest and most award winning winery in Placer County with a spectacular variety of hand-crafted wines you are sure to enjoy! You will often find our family and staff happily working the bottling line putting labels on and wax dipping the port that will be sold in the coming weeks. During the early fall, you will find Jim and Ryan and the vineyard workers preparing for harvest. During the days of late September and the month of October, you will find us crushing, pressing, racking and punching down the new wines!! The evening is spent in a candle lit cave enjoying our sumptuous wines hand selected by our winemaker and paired with a wonderful five to six course menu that our premier Chef prepares for these elegant evenings. TODAY'S PRODUCER · NOVEMBER 20, 2026 BREWBILT BREWING · GRASS VALLEY, CA BrewBilt Brewing GRASS VALLEY, CA · BREWERY In May of 2025, BrewBilt Brewing took a gold medal at the Brewers Cup of California. A few months later the front page of their website said they were winding down. Both of those things are true, and anyone trying to understand what happened in craft beer over the last five years should sit with that for a minute. BrewBilt started in 2021 in Grass Valley, up in the Sierra foothills, and it started from an unusual place. The brewery grew out of BrewBilt Manufacturing, a company that handcrafts custom brewhouses and fermentation systems for other people's breweries. So the founders were not homebrewers who scaled up. They were the people who built the equipment, who knew every weld and every valve on the floor, and then decided to find out what they could make with it. We specialize in small-batch, locally sourced fruit wines. | Swiftwater Wine - Wild Wines From the Alaskan Wilderness | Swiftwater Wines | Skip to content Home Our Products Special Events Contact Us swiftwaterco@gmail.com (907) 521-3576 (opens in new tab) (opens in new tab) “Hand Picked With Love” Welcome! Established in 2023, Swiftwater Wine is a family-run winery based in Wasilla, Alaska. We specialize in small-batch fruit wines made from locally sourced ingredients, thoughtfully crafted to highlight the unique flavors of Alaska while using minimal preservatives and ethically sourced fruit. Our Wines Black Currant Buy Now Deep, earthy tartness of black currants is beautifully balanced by its natural sweetness. Rhubarb Buy Now The crisp tartness of rhubarb unfolds into a smooth, delicate finish, reminiscent of fresh summer fruit. Saint Augustine Buy Now Indulge in the sweet flavors raspberries and tangy rhubarb with our Saint Augustine Raspberry Rhubarb wine. Solstice Sunrise Buy Now Our Solstice Sunrise is an Apple Rhubarb wine with added citrus notes from local spruce tips. "My boyfriend and I went there late in Friday and ended up getting three bottles. We have been meaning to go back but, never catch open hours. Plan to go this weekend, would recommend this wine to anyone near Wasilla or love a different kind of wine. A perk is the owner is lovely as well!" "10/10 experience with the owner and company! the wines are all exceptional, especially the sweet black currant which is my absolute favorite!" "Wonderfully crafted wines, love the Rhubarb - so light, tart and refreshing!" Love that it is all locally made with local fruits and flowers. Kaylee is amazing and so is her wine! So excited that there is now a winery in the Valley! Can't wait to watch this business grow and flourish. Saint Augustine is my favorite blend so far and my Swiftwater hoodie is so comfy! If you're in the Valley, you MUST stop by and grab a bottle when they're open!" "My boyfriend and I went there late in Friday and ended up getting three bottles. We have been meaning to go back but, never catch open hours. Plan to go this weekend, would recommend this wine to anyone near Wasilla or love a different kind of wine. A perk is the owner is lovely as well!" "10/10 experience with the owner and company! the wines are all exceptional, especially the sweet black currant which is my absolute favorite!" 1 2 3 4 5 Want to share your Swiftwater experience? Leave a Review (opens in new tab) Our Beginning Kaylee and KC’s story begins back in Kodiak Alaska, well over a decade ago. Kaylee grew up on a remote island--on the island--living a subsistence lifestyle hunting, fishing, and gardening. For her parents, this also meant making their own wine from fruits they picked locally. Kaylee continued this practice when she moved to Wasilla to be with her now-husband KC. Fast forward a few years; with continued support from family and friends, they work together to gather local fruits from various locations across Alaska as well as local farms. Their goal is to provide Alaska fresh wine that is ethically sourced, supports other Alaskans, and has minimal preservatives. Our First Year Our story began with a dream to share the incredible flavors of Alaska through small batches of hand-crafted wine. In December 2023, we opened our doors for the very first time, and the response was beyond what we could have imagined--our soft opening sold out in under 48 hours! This past year has been an adventure filled with lessons learned, hundreds of pounds of wild and local fruit harvested, and yes, more wine than we'd like to admit was spilled along the way. But overall, it has been an amazing journey, and we cannot thank our community enough. We are truly grateful and can't wait to see what this next year brings. Cheers! Steeped in art, history and a sense of place, locations range from neighborhood pubs to historic hotels where live music and history talks are the norm, and soaking pools, movie theaters and other fun prevail. Handcrafted McMenamins Breweries 68,500+ BATCHES AND COUNTING! McMenamins currently operates 24 breweries, with our newest at Elks Temple in Tacoma, Washington. Since our first brew in 1985, McMenamins has produced more than 68,000 batches. DISCOVER OUR BREWERIES Edgefield Winery STOP BY OUR WINERY TASTING ROOM Founded in 1990, our Edgefield Winery crafts a diverse assortment of wines and ciders, all offered throughout McMenamins eclectic neighborhood pubs and gathering spots in Oregon and Washington. DISCOVER OUR WINERY Coffee Roasters STOP BY FOR A CUP O' JOE! McMenamins approaches specialty coffee roasting with the same passion for attention to detail that we apply to our ales, wines and spirits. Our roast masters use only beans from the highest-quality coffea arabica species – plants that produce coffees of elegant, complex flavors. DISCOVER OUR COFFEE Distilleries HANDCRAFTED SPIRITS Both McMenamins distilleries, one at Edgefield in Troutdale, Ore. and the other at Cornelius Pass Roadhouse in Hillsboro, are now producing heavenly spirits of the highest order, from gins to whiskeys to brandies and more. LOCATIONS, RECIPES AND MORE Discover our Art Take a look at the incredible artwork that adorns our walls, ceilings, floors, doors and more at our pubs, breweries and hotels. Who thinks up this stuff? Who creates it? What is the inspiration? Originally, the artwork served a practical purpose – as Mike McMenamin puts it, "We had good-sized walls to cover." But over the course of twenty-plus years, the art evolved into an expression of the building's history, the company's mission and of McMenamins itself. Browse by Location Get Lost in Our History Our goal is to keep the past in the present, to celebrate and connect us all with the people and events that have helped define each McMenamins property. Steeped in art, history and a sense of place, locations range from neighborhood pubs to historic hotels where live music and history talks are the norm, and soaking pools, movie theaters and other fun prevail. Handcrafted McMenamins Breweries 68,500+ BATCHES AND COUNTING! McMenamins currently operates 24 breweries, with our newest at Elks Temple in Tacoma, Washington. Since our first brew in 1985, McMenamins has produced more than 68,000 batches. DISCOVER OUR BREWERIES Edgefield Winery STOP BY OUR WINERY TASTING ROOM Founded in 1990, our Edgefield Winery crafts a diverse assortment of wines and ciders, all offered throughout McMenamins eclectic neighborhood pubs and gathering spots in Oregon and Washington. DISCOVER OUR WINERY Coffee Roasters STOP BY FOR A CUP O' JOE! McMenamins approaches specialty coffee roasting with the same passion for attention to detail that we apply to our ales, wines and spirits. Our roast masters use only beans from the highest-quality coffea arabica species – plants that produce coffees of elegant, complex flavors. DISCOVER OUR COFFEE Distilleries HANDCRAFTED SPIRITS Both McMenamins distilleries, one at Edgefield in Troutdale, Ore. and the other at Cornelius Pass Roadhouse in Hillsboro, are now producing heavenly spirits of the highest order, from gins to whiskeys to brandies and more. LOCATIONS, RECIPES AND MORE Discover our Art Take a look at the incredible artwork that adorns our walls, ceilings, floors, doors and more at our pubs, breweries and hotels. Who thinks up this stuff? Who creates it? What is the inspiration? Originally, the artwork served a practical purpose – as Mike McMenamin puts it, "We had good-sized walls to cover." But over the course of twenty-plus years, the art evolved into an expression of the building's history, the company's mission and of McMenamins itself. Box 195 Shandon, CA 93461 | group bottle photo of tarica zinfandel, cabernet sauvignon and erlort | tarrica wines, sirah, pinot noir, cabernet sauvignon, merlot and zinfadnel | HOME | WINES | TRADE | ABOUT US | THE WINERY | PRESS/AWARDS | CONTACT US Welcome to Tarrica Wine Cellars Tarrica Wine Cellars is a small, family owned winery started in 2000 in the Paso Robles Wine Country. The focus of our winery is to produce value priced wines that are a clear expression of viticultural origin and varietal flavor. The winery released its first bottled wine in April of 2003. Our wines are available at selected restaurants, markets, and wine shops located on California’s Central Coast, and in the San Francisco Bay Area, Southern California, Colorado, Florida, Alabama, Texas, Pennsylvania, Delaware, Maine, Illinois, North Carolina and South Carolina, Kentucky, Ohio, Michigan and Indiana. The Paso Robles Wine Region Tarrica Wine Cellars farms and sources grapes primarily in the Paso Robles viticultural area, which is ideally situated for growing premium varietal wine grapes. Nestled slightly inland, the warm, clear days are insulated from clouds, fog, and severe winds so sufficient heat reaches the grapes. Following sunset, a marine layer moves over the region and cools temperatures approximately 50 degrees, providing conditions conducive to maintaining outstanding acid structure and overall balance. Most consider this fluctuation to be a key component to the varietal character displayed in the resulting wines. (805) 237-8693 • 111 Clark Road, Shandon, CA 93461

cd7gysp.txt: Cayuse Vineyards – Biodynamic wines from the Walla Walla Valley | The Bionic Lunch dining setup | Cayuse logo | Two hands cradling clipped grape vines | Bionic Wines - Join us for lunch | Cayuse Vineyards produces critically-lauded biodynamic wines including Syrah, Cabernet Sauvignon, Cabernet Franc, Merlot, Grenache, Tempranillo and Viognier. | Cayuse Vineyards The Stones hold the secret Perhaps you’ve heard the almost mythical story, how the brash, young French Vigneron visited the then little-known town called Walla Walla, and fell in love with a few acres of seemingly useless, stone-covered farmland. While the nay-sayers nayed, Christophe Baron deftly turned that field of stones into the acclaimed Cayuse Vineyards. And the rest, as they say, is history—and a whole lot of spectacular wine. Cayuse is a domaine located in the Stones of the Walla Walla Valley. Over the past 20 years, Christophe has made it his mission to craft food-friendly wines of incredible depth, individuality and character—all from fruit grown entirely using biodynamic farming methods. Cayuse creates at least a dozen critically-lauded wines each year, available as wine futures to the Cayuse mailing list. Though that list is currently full, click here to add your name to our wait list. “While the ship has long since sailed with regards to getting on the mailing list, these are singular wines well worth the effort to track down on the secondary market.” —Jeb Dunnuck, The Wine Advocate ©2026 Cayuse VineyardsPO Box 1602, Walla Walla, WA 99362 (509) 526-0686 Contact us

DISCOVER Goold Hill Estate Established 1910 ━━━━━ A Legacy Rooted in the land. Established by the Goold family in 1910, Goold Hill Estate is home to Goold Hill Apple Orchard and Goold Hill Vineyard & Cidery, where you can enjoy apple picking, handcrafted cider, estate wines, and fresh bakery favorites. Explore Honoring a 116-Year Legacy While Looking Ahead For more than a century, this orchard has been a cherished part of the Capital Region. Now, Goold Hill Estate begins an exciting new chapter under the ownership of agricultural entrepreneurs Neviana Zhgaba and Ardian Llomi, founders of the award-winning Aquila's Nest Vineyards. Today, the estate welcomes visitors to experience its renewed offerings while preserving the character and traditions that have made it a beloved destination for generations. From seasonal orchard activities and fresh-baked treats to live music, family-friendly events, and more, Goold Hill Estate celebrates a renewed connection to the land and the community. As part of the restoration, the existing 90-acre orchard is undergoing extensive pruning and revitalization to bring it back to full production. At the same time, the property will welcome new vineyard plantings, continuing the winemaking history once established by Brookview Station Winery and laying the foundation for future estate-grown wines.Neviana and Ardian have successfully transformed farms before. In 2016, they took a vacant 41-acre property in Connecticut and built Aquila's Nest Vineyards into one of the state's premier destinations. Today, the vineyard has been recognized as Connecticut's Best Vineyard, named National Small Producer Winery of the Year, and selected by the U.S. Chamber of Commerce as one of America's Top 70 Small Businesses.At Goold Hill Estate, the vision is simple: preserve what makes this property special while creating new opportunities for families, visitors, and the local community to enjoy it for years to come. Read more Our Orchard ━━━━━ Preserving the Capital Region's oldest family-owned apple orchard since 1910 with care, and respect for the land. Our Vineyard ━━━━━ 7,500 new vineyard plantings will continue the estate's winemaking legacy, laying the foundation for future wines. Our Experiences ━━━━━ Seasonal apple picking, farm events, live entertainment, and memorable gatherings for visitors of all ages. Our Future ━━━━━ Building a destination where agriculture, hospitality, and community come together for generations to enjoy. NOW OPEN AT GOOLD HILL ESTATE ━━━━ Goold Hill Estate is now open and welcoming guests to experience the next chapter of our historic farm. Visitors can now enjoy: • Live music, events, workshops, and artisan markets • A reimagined Farm Store & Cidery with special events • Seasonal baked goods, treats, and locally crafted ciders • New vineyard plantings as we begin our journey toward future Estate wines OPPORTUNITIES AT GOOLD HILL ━━━━ Work with us, perform, or bring your business to the estate. cc4vq0b.txt: HOME | scratchbeer | top of page | | Site | | Social Bar | Facebook - White Circle | Facebook - White Circle | Instagram - White Circle | Instagram - White Circle | SERVICES | | | Anchor 2 | ABOUT US | Marika and Aaron (Photo Credit_ Scratch Brewing Company)_edited.jpg | | Anchor 1 | | BEER & FOOD LIST | | | HOMEBREWER'S ALMANAC | EVENTS | CONTACT | | | | Slideshow | Forage some news | Social Bar | White Twitter Icon | White Twitter Icon | Facebook - White Circle | Facebook - White Circle | Instagram - White Circle | Instagram - White Circle | bottom of page | HOME | scratchbeer | scratchbeer | Skip to Main Content HOME ABOUT MENU HOMEBREWER'S ALMANAC RENT SCRATCH CONTACT & HOURS NEWS FIND STORE ​ ​ Hours ​ Thanksgiving weekend we are open our normal hours:​ Friday - Sunday 12 pm - 8 pm ​​ ​ ​ southern illinois microbrewery & farm open for on-site enjoyment Fri-Sun. to-go orders available by appointment mon-thurs info@scratchbeer.com cash only we do not allow buses. parties of 12 or more please call ahead ABOUT Scratch Brewing Company is a farmhouse brewery located five miles from the Shawnee National Forest in Ava, Illinois. Named one of the top four breweries for foraged beer by Outside Magazine, and one of the most beautiful places to drink beer in the world by All About Beer Magazine, Scratch Brewing Company focuses on farmhouse beers and other styles brewed with estate-grown and foraged ingredients. The brewery has an ever rotating selection of styles enhanced by the innovative addition of local ingredients, such as nettle, elderberry, ginger, dandelion, maple sap, hickory, lavender, juniper, and chanterelle mushrooms. Owners Marika Josephson and Aaron Kleidon create beer whose aim is to showcase the “terroir” of Southern Illinois. For their efforts, they have been nominated for four James Beard Awards, most recently in 2025 for Outstanding Professionals in Beverage Service. The New York Times called Scratch one of the Top 22 pizza places in the United States and "worth a road trip." Their book, The Homebrewers Alamanac, has become an indispensible guide to those seeking more information on brewing with native plants. Beer Advocate said that its "stunning photography makes this book a high-end addition to your homebrew library." Scratch bottles special release offerings and distributes beer to select bars and liquor stores in Illinois and in half a dozen other states. The brewery also supports local artists and artisans, commissioning original ceramics, t-shirts, posters, bottle openers, and other merchandise. In 2017 it opened the Serpent Room, a collaborative project with artist Brett Douglas Hunter, who brought the room to life with his original floor-to-ceiling art and sculptures. The Serpent Room is available to rent for private events and for non-profits; more information is available below. Draft List for November 27 - 29 we are cash only! *all prices include tax* Try a flight of any 4 for $13 hickory bitter ($6 goblet/$17 growler fill) rustic English pub-style ale brewed with hickory leaves from our property and Illinois-grown Crystal hops. easy-drinking with a tannic backboone and earthy spice character from the hops and leaves. 5.0% abv smoked lager ($6 goblet/$17 growler fill) easy-drinking blonde lager brewed with pilsner and a touch of Munich malt, with a hint of smoked barley from Sugar Creek Malt’s wood-fired sainnhus. 5.6% abv sumac cherry saison ($6 goblet/$17 growler fill) farmhouse ale brewed with wild foraged sumac and black cherry tree bark. bubbly with notes of tart cherry and a dry, woodsy finish 5.2% abv strawberry ginger sour ($6 snifter/$17 growler fill)sour ale bewed with local strawberries and fresh ginger in the boil, and fermented with our house sourdough culture. tart and refreshing with a light fruity finish 5.1% abv sassafras lager ($6 goblet/$17 growler fill) a smooth and effervescent light pilsner-style lager brewed with sassafras leaves from our property. light and refreshing with a touch of citrus aroma from the sassafras. 5.0% ​ basil saison ($6 goblet/no growler fill – we have bottles) an effervescent and refreshing farmhouse beer brewed with a large dose of lemon basil from our property. notes of lemongrass, citronella, and sweet basil with a snappy, dry finish. 5.6% abv fennel porter ($6 goblet/$17 growler fill) robust porter brewed with fennel from our garden. Full-bodied with notes of rich chocolate and a touch of sweet anise aroma on the finish. 5.4% abv beet weiss ($6 snifter/$17 growler fill) berliner weiss-style sour beer brewed without hops and dosed in the fermenter with 80 lbs of our own freshly harvested beets. refreshing tartness with an earthy finish and a brilliant pink color. guaranteed to make everyone in the room wonder what you're drinking! 3.8 % abv hickory sour ($6 snifter/$17 growler fill) a sour beer brewed without hops, flavored with a touch of toasted hickory bark, and fermented with our house sourdough culture 5.1% abv non-alcoholic: coffee from dark matter coffee, chicago ($5) * sumac-elderberry-cedar soda ($4) ​ ​ Bottles We have cold bottles available for enjoying here and bottles available at cellar temp to-go ​ black cherry ($17) sour black ale brewed with wild cherry bark harvested from the woods around our brewery and fermented with our wild house mixed culture. Beer is more than a beer, it's an experience. | OUR STORYEVENTS MONTHLY EVENTS VENUE BREWERY MENUCONTACT 0 ENJOYING LIFE THROUGH BEER Beer is more than beer—it’s an experience. At Great Escape, our beer is inspired by an adventurous lifestyle for people who want to savor all life has to offer. We love to experiment and explore the limits of what’s possible in the brewing world, and we strive for excellence because we believe everything is more fun with good beer. Our newest adventure just opened in Republic with a full food & drink menu. Stop by and share a pint - Cheers! OUR MENU NEW LOCATION IS OPEN: 6021 US-HWY, BROOKLINE, MO 65619 Old location on Lone Pine is closed. FIND YOUR ESCAPE WHAT’S ON TAP INSPIRED BY NATURE When we tilt our handcrafted tap handles, your pint glass will slosh and swirl with porters, pale ales and pilsners inspired by Mother Nature’s beauty and diversity. As conservation-minded brewers, we cool our boiling wort with city water and then reuse the hot water in our liquor tank. We also give the spent grain to local farmers for feed. Cheers to environmental stewardship! GIVE BACK BEER FOR SPRINGFIELD We get it. Locals want locally brewed beer. They want beer that’s fit for the environment and the season—beer they can take on a hike, to the lake or to the backyard hammock. So we decided to open a brewery for our neighbors, friends and fellow beer lovers we have yet to meet. Our hope is that Great Escape is a place that’s familiar but never boring. A place to try something new or enjoy an old favorite. A place where people know your name but you always meet someone new. We want to take you on our adventure and join you on yours. BREWED FOR QUALITY Great Escape only serves the highest-quality beer. Our seasonal offerings keep things fresh and allow us to experiment with different flavors. Stop by our brewery and sample our newest varieties. Not sure what’s right for you? Ask our brewmaster, Jake, or one of our intrepid bartenders. They’re here to help you find your new favorite beer. It's the best!” — man who flagged our delivery van down on the streets of portland “finally a great dry cider!” — customers of breakside brewing where you can enjoy son of man on draft! apples matter cider apples, like wine grapes, are grown to be fermented. karmijn de sonnaville, muscadet de dieppe, champagne reinette. Names you would never see at the grocery store. these apples bring real flavor, aroma, and texture. use good apples, pressed fresh during the fall harvest, and you don’t need to add a thing. long and slow most american cideries are more factory than farm. They can churn out a new batch of cider in 6 weeks. ours takes 6 months. good things take time. our long and slow fermentation and aging process means less intervention and more flavor. inspired by the basque country in this corner of northern spain, the cider is made for food. the tart acidity and light natural carbonation elevate all things salty, fishy or fatty. an easy thing to fall in love with, and that’s before you see the long pour. Welcome to the Heart of the Valley Nested within our century-old family orchards, Mt. Hood Winery is a place where volcanic soils, warm Oregon sun and cool alpine breezes meet generations of farming heritage. Whether you are finishing a hike through the Gorge or exploring the iconic Hood River Fruit Loop, we invite you to find a seat on our patio, breathe in the views of Wy’East (Mt. Hood) and Klickitat (Mt. Adams), and savor a glass of our award-winning estate wine. Visit & Savor Daily Tasting Room & Patio Hours We are delighted to welcome you, 12:00 PM - 5:00 PM Friday - Wednesday 12:00 PM - 6:00 PM Thursday Walk-ins are always welcome for flights and glass pours on a first-come, first-served basis. Our Location: 2882 Van Horn Drive Hood River, Oregon 97031 Get Directions - Apple Maps Outside Food & Charcuterie Options : Guests are welcome to bring their own food, picnic items, and snacks to enjoy during their visit. We also offer locally sourced build-your-own charcuterie boxes along with a selection of small bite options available for purchase at the tasting room. Planning Your Trip A Place for Everyone We are proud to be a dog-friendly and family-friendly winery. Relax under our pergola or find a spot in our spacious tasting room, we look forward to sharing our harvest with you. Groups & Gatherings To ensure the best possible experience for all our guests, we ask that parties of 6 or more contact us in advance. For large groups and tour buses, a scheduled appointment is required so we can prepare a dedicated space for your tasting. Call to Inquire - (541) 386-8333 or email hallie@mthoodwine.com Train Schedule Reservation Policy Due to our partnership with the Mount Hood Railroad, we do not accept reservations during scheduled train stop times at the winery. During these periods, the winery may experience very high traffic levels, with trains bringing up to 300 guests per stop, depending on the day . Walk-ins are still welcome, and we offer a condensed menu featuring bottles, glass pours, and three-wine tasting flights during train hours. Please view the Train Schedule on our Groups & Bookings Page when planning your visit. Reserve for 6+ Guests Join Us in The Tasting Room Open daily for flights and glass pours. Take in the dual views of Mt. Hood and Mt. Adams from our patio or relax by the fireplace. Reserve A Table (6+ People) Summit Wine Club Join our family for exclusive releases, member-only events, and a deeper connection to the Century Farm. Join Our Summit Club Live Music Every Thursday | April through October Music typically begins at 4:00 PM and continues until 6:00 PM. All performances are complimentary for our tasting room guests. Live Music Lineup Wine Shop From our 2016 "Winery of the Year" Pinot Noir to our signature Pear Bubbly, bring the taste of Hood River Valley home. Our Wine List Our Wines Estate Pinot Noir Reserve The pinnacle of our estate vineyards, this Pinot Noir is crafted from a rigorous selection of our finest barrels and aged in 50% new French oak from the legendary Alain Fouquet cooperage. It opens with inviting aromas of ripe red fruit, delicate floral notes, and subtle spice. On the palate, layers of vibrant berry, earthy nuance, and gentle oak unfold with depth and balance, carried by a silky texture and refined structure. The finish is long and graceful, leaving a lingering impression of fruit, spice, and polished tannin. A wine made for lingering conversations, quiet reflection, or an exceptional steak. Full Winelist Pinot Noir Crafted predominantly from the premium Pommard clone grown on our estate vineyards, this Pinot Noir is designed around exceptional quality and pigment. COLLINS HOME OUR STORY TAPROOM GUIDELINES CURRENTLY POURING STORE CALENDAR/FOOD TRUCKS ABOUT US CONTACT US MEET THE STAFF FRESH CRAFT BEER IN FORT COLLINS, COLORADO × CRAFTED WITH LOVE × OUR STORY If you're looking for an authentic, one-of-a-kind Northern Colorado beer experience, look no further. Founded in 2018, and expanding to Fort Collins in 2024, our goal from the beginning was to make the best beer in Colorado and instill ourselves into the vibrant community that has supported us over the years. HOW WE STARTED Just like a great new beer, Timnath Beerwerks started out as a fortuitous blend of the right ingredients resulting in an amazing partnership. Three individuals with completely different stories were introduced to one another by pure luck, and realized an opportunity to build a brewery that could be unique, special, and fun. With Pete's background in construction and development, Mike's in real estate and philanthropy, and Cy's in manufacturing and brewing, we set out to make a positive impact through world-class beer. We strive every day to support our amazing family of employees, to foster growth and innovation within our thriving community, to collaborate within the amazing brewing industry in Northern Colorado, and to give back in focused and meaningful ways. ABOUT THE BEER Our beer is brewed first and foremost with quality in mind. When it comes to quality at Timnath Beerwerks, there is no compromise. We subscribe to the belief that making the best beer requires a dance between art and science, with a healthy dose of fun (and delicious) experimentation thrown in for good measure. Our taps change weekly as we rotate through our small-batch, handcrafted ales and lagers. While most of our beers pay homage to the deep-rooted traditions in German and American brewing techniques, we love putting a bit of flair into our recipes to set them apart in unique ways. Finally, we always strive to brew with the freshest and highest-quality ingredients available and take immense pride in supporting the local maltsters and other ingredient suppliers in our Colorado community. ABOUT THE BREWERY Best known for our original Timnath, CO location, we expanded to the Northern Fort Collins brewery district in July 2024 with the acquisition of Snowbank Brewing. This was a natural next step for our operation, allowing us to expand not only our taproom space but also our brewing capacity. We look forward to welcoming the Snowbank community as we grow into the future. GIVING BACK Since we first lit the fire on the brew kettle for our first batch of beer, it has been part of our mission to give back through focused philanthropic efforts that drive positive change in the lives of those in our community who need it most. We take immense pride in our work to date that has helped us donate to charities such as Partners Mentoring Youth, the Boys and Girls Club of Larimer County, ChildSafe, and the Left Hand Foundation. Taproom Guidelines CURRENT GUIDELINES AND SERVICE AT THE TAPROOM Service Expectations We offer counter-service for all beverage and snack orders. Our helpful and friendly staff would love to help you find your next favorite style of beer from our tap list, which contains a variety of flagships, seasonals, and rotating styles alike! Outside Food and Beverage We like to support our local community by partnering with local food trucks when possible! Outside food is always allowed, but we encourage our guests to try the local faire when a food truck is present. A variety of non-alcoholic beverages is also offered - we ask that you please limit outside beverages to water. Pets Per ADA guidelines, Service Animals are always welcomed on our premises. Well-behaved pets are always welcomed to the taproom, as long as they remain on a leash and with their owner while visiting our establishment. We kindly ask to be aware of your surroundings and be courteous to other animals and people around you! We reserve the right to remove any owners and their animals from the premises due but not limited to aggressive or reactive behavior. Children Children are always welcome to our taproom! We only ask that children remain supervised by their parents while visiting the taproom. We do provide kid-friendly, non-alcoholic options available for purchase. We also have a small selection of games and activities for kiddos and adults alike! If you need any equipment for the games and activities, we ask that the parents accompany their child to the bar for permission to use the equipment and that the children remain under close supervision while using our equipment. Closed for Summer Break September 8-14 Returning to regular hours Tuesday September 15, 2026 Parts & Labor Brewing Company is in the business of beer- and not just any beer. We build great beer. Parts & Labor Brewing Co. handcrafts all its beers inside the doors of a renovated, century- old Cadillac dealership repair shop. It's been a few years since those cars have rolled out of here, but owners Dylan & Kimberly Harford keep the memory alive with a vintage shop vibe and beers that have won them both the hearts of many locals, as well as some pretty prestigious recognition within the craft beer culture. PHONE (970) 425-7540 LOCATION 402 Main Street Unit B Sterling, Colorado 80751 HOURS T-Th 11a-9p F-Sa 11a–10p Su 12p-8p M Closed Some of the beers we’ve had in the past… (Check the ‘Tapped’ tab at the top of this page for current tap list) Camshaft Kolsch Light in color with malty character. Slightly dry, crisp finish. A great place to start. ABV: 5.7% Split Decision Coffee Kolsch When you only have one mug- coffee or beer? How ‘bout both. We fermented our classic kolsch with some arabica for a mellow coffee or a high-octane beer. Whatever you call it, it makes for a great day. ABV: 5.7% Haas Local Wheat Featuring locally sourced wheat from the Haas family, this beer is light-bodied and its aromatic yeast yields a light, often fruity character and inherent cloudiness. Haas is an entire series of wheat beers including American, German, Belgian, and Bavarian styles- ask your beertender which one is on tap. ABV: 6.3% Red Rooster Imperial Red Ale Well-balanced hop and malt character, it is a high-octane beer that is surprisingly easy to drink. Solid, approachable red. ABV: 9.3% Redneck Mother Citrus IPA Not overly hoppy, this IPA features Centennial and Citra hops that gives it a fruity character. A really good IPA in this super popular citrus style. ABV: 6.9% Redneck Stepmother Citrus IPA Just like its predecessor, except this time it features Citra, Galaxy and Amarillo hops to give it a complex and fruity hop character. ABV: 6.9% Loose Lips Sink Ships Vanilla Coconut Porter Robust malt flavor harmonizes with hops, notes of cocoa and caramel. Malty with flavors of vanilla, tobacco and coconut. ABV: 7.2% Cherry Poppins Montmorency Cherry Sour Ale Our popular kettle sour is back! Fermented and conditioned on fresh Montmorency cherries from Michigan, it's perfectly tart, has a crisp mouthfeel and plenty of pie cherry flavor- truly delightful! ABV: 6.5% Shotgun Willie Nelson Sauvin Hazy Double IPA This one is a treat! Dry-hopped with copious amounts of Nelson Sauvin hops, giving it tons of tropical fruit flavor, with a creamy mouthfeel. Haze abounds in this big beer. ABV: 9.3% Canada Wet Double Brown (Cask Conditioned on Canadian Maple Syrup) A malt bomb for your mouth, this brown ale is cask-conditioned on real Canadian maple syrup. It's caramely, mapley, and very delicious! ABV: 9.8% Rantallion Red IPA Floral, fruity and piney- a super aromatic brew. All about hop flavor with this one- by far the most popular craft beer style in the US. We think ours is pretty good, too. ABV: 7.7% My Soviet Friend Imperial Stout Strongest in alcohol and body. Rich, malty flavor and aroma complimented by just enough hop character. Strong cocoa and coffee flavors. A serious beer for serious beer drinkers. ABV: 13.2% You Can't Get There from Here NEIPA Hazy IPA packed with flavor-fruity character imparted by the hops, yet the finish is creamy with little to no bitterness. One of our favorites! ABV: 6.2% A Particular Set of Skills Pale Ale A golden amber color, medium body and slight fruitiness from the hops, this pale ale has an aromatic finish that showcases the inherent hop character. Give it a shot- it's pretty tasty. ABV: 5.4% Afternoon Delight Strawberry Blonde This is our easy drinker! Blondes are known for not having a dominating character- neither overly malty nor hoppy- it is pleasing in aroma, body and flavor. Ours is taken up a notch by an infusion of fresh strawberries that aren't overpowering but give you the essence of a strawberry warmed by the sun dropped right in. ABV: 5.7% M'Lady Earl Grey Saison Complex flavors come from the yeast in this Belgian-style ale. Fruity and flavorful from the Earl Grey tea infusion, this is one to remember. ABV: 6.1% My Sister's Side Hustle Belgian Wit This beer features our favorite local unmalted wheat and gets some delicious esters from the yeast as well as an infusion of bitter orange peel. ABV: 7.1% Meringue-A-Tang Lemon Meringue Pie IPA A "twist" on a familiar IPA- this lemony delicious beer has over 20 pies smashed right in, balancing the hop bitterness with a sweet lemon treat! ABV: 7.1% Bramblebunny Blackberry Sage Rye IPA This one has a lot goin' on! Tangy and fruity from the blackberries and rye mash, and earthy from the sage with the traditional aroma and finish of the ever-popular IPA. A true delight for the senses, but not for the faint of heart! ABV: 6.8% Fireside Chat Imperial Red Ale This Imperial Red Winter Ale has a well-balanced hop and malt character. A solid, caramely beer in the American Imperial Red- style. ABV: 10.6% Liquid Lunchbox Peanut Butter & Jelly Stout Sounds a bit crazy, but boy, oh boy is it

Try a different browser. At Lost Abbey, we believe great beer is a creative act—that is defined by art, crafted through devotion resulting in a shared experience. Our beers are contemplative companions, brewed with reverence for those who came before us and those who gather with us now. In Illa Brettanomyces Nos Fides Explore Lost Abbey beers Find your sanctuary in every pour A Higher Order of Brewing Our devotion to the craft has earned international recognition. Beers like Duck Duck Gooze, Carnevale, and Devotion have been celebrated on the world’s biggest stages, while our co-founder Tomme Arthur received the Russell Scherer Award for Brewing Innovation, one of the highest honors in American brewing. These awards are milestones, not the mission—markers along a longer path of craft, creativity, and brewing for sinners and saints alike. About The Lost Abbey Stories from the Abbey October 20, 2026 Tomme’s 30th Anniversary and… Read more → June 11, 2026 Please welcome to The Lost Abbey Hospitality Family The Monastery. Our Tasting Room is where you will find some of the most passionate and enthusiastic of our followers. Heated patio, event space, and our largest selection of vintage offers. Make the Vista Pilgrimage The Sanctuary - San Marcos Peace be with brew. Nestled in the hills of North County, The Sanctuary offers a serene escape from the noise of the world. This family-friendly refuge is where locals gather to share food, stories, and fresh pours under the open sky. A place to slow down, connect, and celebrate life’s simpler sacraments. Food trucks Wed-Sun. Make the San Marcos Pilgrimage The Monastery - Miralani District A place for quiet contemplation and exceptional beer. Nestled within the Miralani Makers' District, The Monastery offers a more contemplative side of The Lost Abbey experience. Inspired by the warmth of an English pub, this intimate gathering place invites guests to settle into a sofa, challenge a friend to darts, and linger over thoughtfully crafted beers. Make the Miralani District Pilgrimage The Confessional - Cardiff Where the faithful come to confess their thirst. A short walk from the ocean, The Confessional is equal parts coastal hideaway and spiritual experience. The confessional booth invites beachgoers and believers alike to unburden themselves over a pint. Here, every sip is an act of repentance—best followed by another. Make the Cardiff Pilgrimage The Church - San Diego Raise your glass beneath vaulted shadows. Experience the best Lost Abbey has to offer. Our large deck is perfect for events at Petco. Doggos Gus provides TJ Style Dogs and Smash Burgers. Make the San Diego Pilgrimage The Conduit Every month we share tales from the brewery, upcoming gatherings, and rare offerings reserved for those who seek them. Because good beer, like good faith, is best when shared. cqqq682.title: Eventide Brewing | Great Doesn't Have to Be Complicated
cqqq682.txt: Eventide Brewing | Great Doesn't Have to Be Complicated | ElDorado IPA | Eventide Kölsch | Eventide Pale Ale | Eventide Stout | Highlander | Red Headed Haley | Geoffrey Williams | Haley Cowan | Mathew Sweezey | Nathan Cowan | Eventide Brewing is an Atlanta craft brewery offering fresh, locally brewed beers, seasonal releases, and a welcoming taproom experience. | Home - Eventide Brewing | Eventide Brewing | Eventide Brewing: Craft Beer in Atlanta Skip to content Eventide Brewing About Store Calendar Map to our beer Gallery Brewery Blog Tasting Room Follow @EventideBrewing Want to know when our next beer hits shelves? Yes? ElDorado IPA Style: IPA | Alcohol: 6.5% APPEARANCE Dark gold color and medium carbonation NOSE Lighter fruit notes are present and a light sweetness from the malt can be detected. Smells like a bouquet of tropical fruits. MOUTHFEEL Medium carbonation with a medium body, slightly sweet finish. TASTING NOTES Showcasing a huge El Dorado hop profile, which imparts tropical fruit notes like mango, lychee, tangerine, and pineapple, the lighter body of this beer allows for a very drinkable IPA that's big enough to pack a punch but light enough to drink on a hot summer's day. ONE OFF STYLE This was a one off style which is no longer in production e·ven·tide /ˈēvənˌtīd/ (Noun) Eventide is an old English term meaning “evening” or “twilight”. For us it represents the time of day that anything is possible and everything is exactly as you want it to be. Our Story Eventide Brewing was formed out of friendship and a love of good beer. Nathan, Haley, and Geoffrey all met at Georgia Southern, and later on began to experiment with homemade pickles, mustard, cheese, and beer. Nathan and Geoffrey’s first batch of beer was brewed on a “Mr. Beer” kit. Shortly after realizing they needed to upgrade, Nathan fabricated a three kettle brew system, which is still used to create our test brews today. Mathew joined the team a few years later after being introduced to the group through one of Haley’s close friends. The combination of everyone’s background and talents has allowed us to build this company from the ground up, become closer friends, and craft award winning beer. We are very happy to call Atlanta home and to provide this great city with offerings that will really show what “Craft” can be. To us, great doesn’t have to be complicated. Members of Eventide Geoffrey Williams He Makes the Beer Geoffrey is the taste and talent behind our products and is the person that keeps production moving along. He knows whose ass to kick (ours) to get product in and out in a timely manner, and he is tasked with making sure the beer makes its way to you. As a thirteen-year veteran of logistics and supply chain management, he knowshow to keep production and our supply chain running. A perfectionist of his craft (pun intended), his recipes go through multiple phases before being finalized and approved for general consumption ensuring that only the highest quality product will ever make it to you. His beers have won multiple awards, and he has recently been granted the honor of becoming a BJCP judge. His approach to the brewing process is best summed up in Vince Lombardi’s statement, “Perfection is not attainable, but if we chase perfection we catch excellence.” This thought is the driving force behind his passion to create and sustain something great -- without all of the complications. Haley Cowan The face Haley works as our brand manager, our “feet on the street.” Sales tops the list of things she’s passionate about, probably because she is ridiculously competitive and good at it-- due to years of experience. When you see her out and about, she’ll have a smile on her face, a determined look in her eye, and, most likely, a pharmacy textbook in hand. She is excited to be close to finishing her Doctorate of Pharmacy at Mercer University. Mathew Sweezey How stuff looks Mathew is responsible for how things look and feel. Our brand is his baby. He started his love affair with creativity when he was a kid playing around in his dad’s wood shop. From there, he got into design, marketing, and art. He's a nationally ranked woodworker, author of books on marketing, and an all around good guy. When he's not being a super marketing dork, you'll likely find him outside. His current sports are longboarding, camping, hunting, and snowboarding. If you meet him, he'll probably be in a ball cap, t-shirt, and a smile. In hisown words, "I love what I do and hope it shows every time you pick up a can of our beer." Nathan Cowan Head Engineer Nathan is the CEO of Eventide Brewing. He has over 10 years of experience in mechanical engineering and construction and is a registered Professional Engineer with the State of Georgia. Nathan’s passion for brewing stems from the complex engineering and coordination involved in the brewing process as well as his interest in business development – and beer. He takes care of the critical project development steps and the challenges of design implementation that keep Eventide Brewery up and running -- and us moving towards our goals. When not running a brewery, Nathan pursues his interest in making things from scratch including homemade mustard, pickles, and home-grown veggies. He counts himself lucky to have Haley as his loving wife and partner in this project. Help Us Give Back We lost a great friend in March of 2012, Cullen Branch. He was an avid hunter, a backpacker, was honored to be Annie Lebowitz’s understudy for 2 years, and, up until the time of his passing, was a camera operator for the hit series Auction Kings. He will be missed, but his legacy will live on with the creation of the “Cullen Branch” memorial grant. This grant will be giving out $100 to organizations who helps people within the Atlanta community, support the arts, or are focused on the outdoors. Help us to keep his memory alive but nominating a charity which you think should be awarded the grant. About Contact 1015 Grant

From train robbers to gamblers’ jackpots, this place serves up a good story alongside pub fare and handcrafted beverages. It’s beginning to look a lot like cocktail hour! Stop by our holiday pop-up bar, The Nightcap Before Christmas, for winter warmers, festive cocktails and holiday cheer in the New Tourist Bar. Opens November 27 Upcoming Events see all events Happy 41st Birthday, Terminator Stout! Tuesday, November 24 Friendsgiving Wednesday, November 25 Thanksgiving - Buffet - To Go Thursday, November 26 The Nightcap Before Christmas Pop-up Bars Friday, November 27 Relax in style amid the legends Walking guide Among hotels in Centralia, Washington, The Olympic Club Hotel's legend looms large. Here you'll find a historic building – filled with warm woods and period details – steeped in colorful tales of countless gamblers' jackpots, revenuer raids, dark secrets deeply buried, and a famous bandit's bravado. The Olympic Club Hotel has been a point of power, intrigue and contention since opening in 1908. Its name evokes heroic gods of ancient Herculean characters, the exploits of whom are now the stuff of modern legend. Remarkably, the Olympic Club Hotel remains virtually unchanged from the time of its opulent remodel in 1913. Still much in evidence is the building's blend of sophisticated finery and earthy extravagance. Its magnificent mahogany bar and leaded-glass canopies are as impressive as the colossal Round Oak wood stove, elegant women's bathroom and mammoth porcelain urinals, (hey, they spared no expense in those bygone days!). The hotel's 27 guest rooms feature vintage furnishings, comfy chenille-covered beds and conveniently located private common bathrooms. You may hear the lonely, soulful sound of the trains from your room as they roll through Centralia – but if you'd prefer not to, earplugs are provided. Each room here is named for the colorful and worthy cast of characters who have left their mark on this place – the internationally notorious "gentleman train robber" Roy Gardner who was captured at the hotel back in 1921; Gertrude Howell, the hotel's first female proprietor who also identified Gardner; and Jack Sciutto, the Oly Club's original proprietor who was crowned "King of Bootleggers." As refined as the Olympic Club Hotel may have been portrayed, especially in its early years, the place has always possessed an element of the Old West with stories of train robbers and ladies of the evening who took up residency on the second floor. Known as a true "gentleman's resort" the opulent furnishings of mahogany paneling, Tiffany-style lights, ceramic-tiled floors and Belgian crystal lured a good many of the area's loggers, miners and railroad workers through the doors. McMenamins has expanded upon the Olympic Club Hotel's traditional definition of a workingman's resort by welcoming the whole family to enjoy lodging, meals, movies, art, history, sport and special events. Throughout the Olympic Club historic photographs and extensive original artwork chronicle the building's intriguing history. We hope you enjoy our cider! | Cidery | Raising Cane Ranch | Raising Cane Ranch | Skip to Main Content RAISING CANE RANCH Cidery Orchard Farm Stays Conservation About More Riverview Road Cidery Tree to Tap​ Raising Cane Ranch grows the apples and fruits that go into making our hard ciders. We specialize in a simple and honest product, nothing fancy. At this point, our cider is a blend of fresh eating, heirloom, and traditional cider apples that we press in the Fall. During fermentation, we add cultured yeast for a balanced flavor profile, yet sometimes we only use the wild yeast from the fruit. Our vision is for customers to come, soak in the chill atmosphere, and enjoy themselves. Most important to us is the connection we have with our customers and that they have with our farm. We hope you enjoy our cider! ​ Take a tour of our cidery in this video! Learn about our new cidery art by local artist Mahllie. Tasting Areas & Hours ​ We converted our old cow barn into a cidery and taproom, with indoor and outdoor seating. Parking is in the UPICK apple orchard. We post current information about the cidery on our social media and Farm News spot on the homepage of this website. ​​​​​​ SEASONALLY OPEN: JUNE - OCTOBER (Friday-Sunday) exact times on Google ​​ Our Ciders CORE TAPS ​ Scrumpy - fermented from wild yeast, complex flavor, different from year to year, dry Dry - fermented with cultured yeast, crisp, completely dry Happy Orchard - fermented with cultured yeast, lightly back-sweetened, balanced, refreshing ROTATING TAPS We create new ciders by adding fruits and botanicals we grow, such as Blackberries, Aronia berries, Tayberries, Plums, Currants, Rhubarb, Concord grapes, Blueberries, Figs, Quince, and other native berries. Using our traditional cider apples, we offer special combinations and single varietals, especially Kingston Black. Riverview Road Cider is only available here on the farm, so bring a growler, and we'll fill it for you! ​ ​ Members of the Northwest Cider Association and the American Cider Association Raising Cane Ranch 5719 Riverview Rd Snohomish, WA 98290 ‭(206) 724-5303‬ info@raisingcaneranch.com Join our mailing list to get farm updates! The main Chandelier shines brightly. | Message | GoDaddy Airo | Wicked Warren's is a brewery located in Warren, PA with a beautiful rustic decor where you can relax and enjoy a beer or wine with awesome wood fired pizza. | Wicked Warren's | Wicked Warren's | Your home for Outstanding Beer, Wood Fired Pizza as well as other culinary delights HOME JAMESTOWN WARREN SHOP MORE Wood Fired Pizza & Fresh Brewery Beer Join us for a Pie & Pint Locations Warren 1-814-433-2739 330 Pennsylvania Ave. W Warren, PA 16365 VISIT WARREN Jamestown 1-716-484-4070 119 West 3rd Street Jamestown, NY 14701 VISIT JAMESTOWN Featured Products About Us Who was "Wicked Warren"? CHAPTER I Born in Germany, Werner Muller came to Elis Island in 1830 at age 23. After receiving his citizenship papers, He followed a man he met on the boat to a small hamlet in Pennsylvania. He became the accountant for the Unified Kerosene company. Over the next 2 years Werner succeeded to embezzle almost $20,000 (Over half million dollars in todays world) from the incredibly successful oil company. His luck ran out on December 23, 1832 when he was caught having relations with the owner's daughter in a supply closet. He was never suspected of the embezzlement. When Warren, PA became incorporated in 1832, just prior to Werner being fired, he cleverly changed his name to Warren and proclaimed that the new city was named after him. His Great, Great, Great, Grandfather was a successful brewer and lawyer in Germany and helped write the famous Reinheitsgebot beer purity laws in Germany. Each Muller generation after perfected the art of Brewing using the laws but never opened a commercial brewery but instead provided their family brew to neighbors and visiting family. Warren had kept the family tradition of brewing as soon as he was established in the Pennsylvania community and decided that he would turn his hobby into a career after being fired. He choose a location on the west side of the river on Pennsylvania Avenue. The brewery became an instant success with lines out the door of people picking up jugs of the brew. After less than a year daily deliveries started heading to Jamestown and Erie. Warren was always flying off the handle at someone, delivery people, suppliers, even customers, but most of all his Master Brewer. It didn’t take long for Warren to gain the nickname “Wicked Warren” among the town’s folk. The Brew Master had had enough after a berating by Warren that turned into a physical altercation. During the altercation the brewer picked up a stirring paddle and beat Warren to death. The Brew Master was so scared, he disposed of Warren by adding him to the in-house Wood Fired Pizza Oven and diminishing him to Ashes. It has long been documented that Warren continues to “Stir the pot” by haunting the old brewery! CHAPTER II Truth be known that the only thing Warren was haunting was the rumors that the Brew Master killed him. You see, there never was any truth to the killing and the Brew Master was never convicted. Come to find out the rumors of Warren’s death was just a cover up so he could escape the reality of a murder that he himself had committed. You see, Warren was still maintaining his affair with the Kerosene owner’s daughter but could not go public with it because her father threatened to kill him if he ever touched his daughter again. Not only was he touching the daughter, but he was also having relations with a woman he met in Jamestown when he was delivering beer up there. The Jamestown women was a beautiful red head that was playful and full of life with a charismatic personality that drew Warren to her immediately. Eveline loved the fact that Warren was a bad boy. The daughter found out about Eveline and confronted Warren immediately which quickly resulted in a heated argument. The daughter threatened Warren that she had had enough and was going to tell her father that he embezzled the money after all. This threw Warren over the edge, and he killed her on the spot and ran away to Jamestown in the middle of the night with nothing but a stolen horse and a bag full of money. After shaving his famous mustache and curly hair Warren maintained a low profile in Jamestown. He Reestablished himself in Jamestown and started another brewery. The new brewery was much larger than the Warren Brewery and was set up to distribute as far north as Buffalo. It seems Warren turned over a new leaf when he moved to Jamestown. Eveline and he were married and had a daughter. They named their beautiful daughter Flora Belle. Will marriage and fatherhood change Warren for good?
